html:
The Battle of Tarawa was fought from 20 to 23 November 1943, when US Marines landed on Betio, a small islet of Tarawa atoll held by Japanese troops.

Landing craft stuck on the reef at low tide, and many Marines were shot wading ashore. In three days about a thousand Americans died, and almost all of the Japanese garrison of several thousand, along with Korean labourers.

The heavy losses shocked the American public and changed how later landings were planned. Tarawa opened the US drive through Micronesia in the Pacific War, towards the Marshalls; see Kwajalein. War remains are still found on Betio. See Gilbert and Ellice Islands.
